newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money slightly up but seen easing.
newsitem.headline: German call money slightly up but seen easing.

text.p: German call money rates firmed slightly to 2.975 to 3.025 percent on Monday from around 2.95 to 3.00 percent on Friday but dealers predicted rates would fall during the day as bank reserves remained high.

Commercial banks' effective deposits at the Bundesbank totalled 42.2 billion marks on Friday, down from 43.1 billion marks on Thursday. while the average for the month through Sunday was 40.6 billion marks, up from 40.4 billion.
That was well above the provisional minimum reserve requirement of 38.7 billion marks for December.

Dealers said banks would not want to maintain such high reserves in non interest-bearing Bundesbank deposits ahead of the Christmas break and may seek to offload funds today, pushing call money rates down.
Lombard borrowings were unchanged at about 100 million marks on Friday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was 3.02075 percent on Monday, up from 2.97567 on Friday.
